sources.title: Structured Interviews: A Practical Guide
sources.setting: Guidance for U.S. federal hiring; read introduction, job-analysis steps, question design and probing sections.
sources.finding: The guide links interview questions to job competencies, distinguishes past-behavior from hypothetical questions, and recommends planned clarification probes and pilot testing.
sources.use: Build a practice question from one JD requirement; ask for an actual incident, personal action and observable outcome. Keep hypothetical plans separate from completed experience.
limits: Employer assessment guidance, not a trial of this Skill or a guarantee of candidate success.
Adaptive coaching does not reproduce a standardized selection interview; do not import its rating scales as personal hiring probabilities.
Historical U.S. federal guidance; local legal requirements require current local sources.
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal hiring guidance; not Chinese employment law
sources.version: September 2008 guide, 36 PDF pages; selected printed pages 3–7 and 12–14 checked

sources.title: The Structured Employment Interview: Narrative and Quantitative Review of the Research Literature
sources.authors: Julia Levashina; Christopher J. Hartwell; Frederick P. Morgeson; Michael A. Campion
sources.setting: Review of employment-interview research on structure, bias, impression management, question types, rating scales, probing and applicant reactions; abstract read.
sources.finding: The review combines narrative discussion with quantitative synthesis where possible and identifies unresolved questions rather than one universally optimal interview format.
sources.use: Make the purpose of each practice question explicit, then clarify the user's actual response. Treat probing design as a choice with tradeoffs; identify coached wording separately from new evidence.
limits: Only the publisher abstract was read; do not cite specific subgroup estimates, tables or moderator results from this card.
Selection-interview research does not establish that LLM coaching improves job offers.
The abstract does not establish transfer to every country, occupation or candidate group.
sources.jurisdiction: Employment research across reviewed settings; country coverage not established from abstract
sources.version: Personnel Psychology 67, 241–293 (2014); online first 10 July 2013; DOI 10.1111/peps.12052

sources.title: Revisiting meta-analytic estimates of validity in personnel selection: Addressing systematic overcorrection for restriction of range
sources.authors: Paul R. Sackett; Charlene Zhang; Christopher M. Berry; Filip Lievens
sources.setting: Reanalysis of earlier personnel-selection validity syntheses, especially corrections for restriction of range; original abstract read through PubMed.
sources.finding: The authors identify overcorrection in earlier approaches and report lower revised validity estimates for many selection procedures; structured interviews rank highly in their reanalysis.
sources.use: Explain why job-related, structured evidence deserves attention while retaining uncertainty. Check correction methods, outcome definitions and variation before repeating historical rankings.
limits: A predictor–job-performance association is not an individual's probability of passing an interview.
A meta-analytic ranking is conditional on included evidence and correction choices, not a universal ranking for every employer.
Abstract-only reading does not settle subsequent methodological debate or subgroup applicability; it does not validate this Skill.
sources.jurisdiction: Personnel-selection literature; do not extrapolate to a particular country or demographic group
sources.version: Journal of Applied Psychology 107(11), 2040–2068 (2022); online first 30 December 2021; DOI 10.1037/apl0000994

sources.title: A Review of Structure in the Selection Interview
sources.authors: Michael A. Campion; David K. Palmer; James E. Campion
sources.setting: Historical review of ways to structure interview content and response evaluation; publisher abstract and bibliographic information checked.
sources.finding: The review identifies fifteen components of interview structure and evaluates them against reliability, validity and user reactions; structure comprises multiple design choices.
sources.use: Separate what a practice question asks from how its answer is reviewed. Record the target competency and missing observable detail instead of issuing an unexplained global candidate score.
limits: The abstract does not provide enough detail to implement or attribute every component; use the official guide for concrete procedures.
This historical review is not a current universal effect-size estimate or a validation of conversational coaching.
Publisher online-posting date differs from the 1997 journal year.
sources.jurisdiction: Selection-interview research; country and occupation coverage not established from abstract
sources.version: Personnel Psychology 50(3), 655–702 (1997); publisher webpage posted 7 December 2006; DOI 10.1111/j.1744-6570.1997.tb00709.x

sources.title: Test-enhanced learning: taking memory tests improves long-term retention
sources.authors: Henry L. Roediger; Jeffrey D. Karpicke
sources.setting: Two experiments with students learning prose passages; immediate free recall versus restudy, followed by retention tests after short or longer delays.
sources.finding: Retrieval produced better delayed retention than additional study, whereas restudy performed better at the shortest delay. Confidence after restudy did not imply better delayed recall.
sources.use: As an explicitly indirect design hypothesis, let the user attempt an answer before showing a rewrite, then revisit the same evidence gap later. Compare concrete answer details rather than confidence alone.
limits: Student prose-memory experiments are not evidence of improved interview performance or hiring outcomes.
Remembering a polished sentence neither verifies its claims nor demonstrates job competence.
Abstract-only reading; country and sample composition are not established here.
sources.jurisdiction: Educational memory experiments; no employment-law applicability

sources.title: The effects of feedback interventions on performance: A historical review, a meta-analysis, and a preliminary feedback intervention theory
sources.setting: Historical synthesis of feedback effects across performance tasks; original abstract read on the author's uploaded publication page, with bibliography checked on the author's site.
sources.finding: Feedback improved performance on average but some effects were negative. The proposed account links effectiveness to where attention is directed, including movement away from the task toward the self.
sources.use: As an indirect coaching design choice, identify one answer-specific gap and one retry action. Avoid personality judgments and stop escalating critique when it no longer helps the user's task.
limits: Diverse performance tasks are not direct evidence of improved job-search or interview outcomes.
Moderator findings do not guarantee that any particular feedback wording will help this user.
Publisher access failed; only the original abstract and author bibliography were read, not the full meta-analysis.
sources.jurisdiction: Performance-feedback research across tasks; sample geography not established from abstract
sources.version: Psychological Bulletin 119(2), 254–284 (1996); DOI 10.1037/0033-2909.119.2.254; author-uploaded abstract accessed
